I am a 52-year-old woman farming in Kagera. Money is tight and this plot is small, only about three-quarters of an acre, so I will not waste my limited cash on chemical fertilizer that the extension officer says works better on big maize fields. I have some cows and goats at home, so I will spread manure on this plot like I always do, and I will plant the same bean and cassava seed I saved from last season because it still grows well here. This plot is close to home, so my children and I can manage the clearing, planting, weeding, and harvesting ourselves without hiring anyone, and we have no way to irrigate it anyway.
